outcome: rate of positive maternal Kleihauer-Betke's (KB) test
cohort: 92 women who underwent cesarean delivery, with 31 having transplacental transection and 61 controls
finding: The study found that while transplacental transection during cesarean delivery did not significantly increase the rate of a positive maternal KB test, it was associated with a higher likelihood of newborn hematocrit <40% at delivery.
mod_finding: This study found that cesarean delivery requiring transplacental transection was not associated with a significantly increased rate of fetomaternal bleeding but was associated with a higher likelihood of newborn hematocrit <40% at delivery.
